title: Placement in Counting Sort
statement: Let $n$, $d_0$, $b$, and $c$ be natural numbers, where $n$ is the number of items, $d_0$ is the base address of the destination region, $b$ is the key bound, and $c$ is the base address of the counter region. Let $k(j)$ be the key of item $j$, let $x(j)$ specify the item at index $j$, and let $m$ be a memory map. For every $t<b$, the counter cell at address $c+t$ contains the number of indices $j<n$ with $k(j)<t$, plus the number of indices $j<i$ with $k(j)=t$. For every $j<i$, the destination cell at address $d_0+	ext{sortPos}(k,n,j)$ contains $x(j)$, where $	ext{sortPos}(k,n,j)$ denotes the sorted position used for item $j$ among the first $n$ items.
hypotheses_covered: For every natural number t < A.nb, μ'(A.cnt + t) equals cntLt kf t A.n plus cntEq kf t i.
For every natural number j < i, μ'(A.dst + sortPos kf A.n j) equals it j.
